Analytics Leader
(noun)
Bridges statistical models with commercial reality, translating business dilemmas into testable hypotheses.
Analytics Culture
(noun)
Transitions organizational decision-making from executive gut feel to disciplined hypothesis testing.
Analytics Capability
(noun)
The collective enterprise maturity across leadership, talent triad, decision culture, and data tooling.
Big Rocks
(noun phrase)
The 3 to 5 enterprise priorities that move top-line revenue, bottom-line costs, or core risk exposures.
D2D (Data-to-Decisions)
(framework acronym)
A structured, closed-loop operating methodology ensuring analytical insights culminate in measurable commercial action.
Data Maturity
(noun phrase)
The developmental journey advancing from backwards-looking descriptive reporting to forward prescriptive action.
Embedded Analytics
(noun phrase)
Hub-and-spoke organizational topology embedding specialized quants directly inside business unit workflows.
Head of Analytics
(executive role)
The enterprise leader balancing portfolio strategy, cross-functional translation, and technical talent architecture.
HIPPO
(acronym)
Highest Paid Person’s Opinion—the systemic corporate anti-pattern of defaulting to seniority over verified empirical data.
Pullable Levers
(noun phrase)
Specific operational controls (pricing tiers, channel mix, defect tolerances) that directly alter financial outcomes.
Stakeholder
(noun)
Key operators, budget owners, and executives whose frontline buy-in dictates whether analytical models are adopted.
Business Impact
(noun phrase)
The bottom-line commercial return that justifies the data science and engineering investment.
Quick Win
(noun phrase)
A high-impact, 30-day proof of concept delivering early executive credibility and momentum.
Prescriptive Analytics
(noun phrase)
Advanced mathematical optimization identifying not just what will happen, but exactly what decision to execute.
